<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **75** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/position.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**55** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/position.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 40 pages)`
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6055aa67ff09e716051a47ba2f3d5648aa0704db` — the merge of head `9b3d8b8169fd170b316d7fda7ea7a0c5907caca6` into base `64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6055aa67ff09e716051a47ba2f3d5648aa0704db && git checkout 6055aa67ff09e716051a47ba2f3d5648aa0704db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027 9b3d8b8169fd170b316d7fda7ea7a0c5907caca6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027 && git merge --no-ff 9b3d8b8169fd170b316d7fda7ea7a0c5907caca6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 64c426ab22aa1f13290240aff1cd02dc1bf56027` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d9befe7f9ff249c3b99789579052e623632ed5e4`
Local-runs: probe — the declaration-line readers in scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs were run over the PR body and the changeset, as the order allowed; nothing was built and no test was run
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/position-renamed-from.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.test.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/position-renamed-from.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/position.json, packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/position.md, packages/spec/authorable-surface/identity.json, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md, content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx (the generated counts only), .changeset/32983-position-renamed-from-carries-holders.md (declaration lines only)

Read, not reviewed (outside the diff): `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-position.object.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/stored-permission-set-package-backfill.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-metadata-activation.object.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/package-state-store.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (the field `renamedFrom` doctrine), `packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts`, ADR-0150 D1, D7 and D8, card #32983 with the dev report 6841803143, the decision analysis 6841869138, the ruling 6841971722, the claims 6841987296 and 6843365364, the dev report 6843412313, the PR body, and hotcrm PR #2446 `scripts/migrate-position-holders.ts` at its merge commit. The changeset prose, the reference page and the PR body are prose faces: the seat's ACCEPT, not this record. The dev's suite counts and ablations are the dev's readings. Also run, read-only: `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` for the Scope hits, and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (no major). `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` could not run without an install, so no reading was taken from it. Check-runs on this head when read: 40 success, 10 skipped, 1 failure (`Test Core (6/8)`), 14 in progress, 65 in all. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). The PR is a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Holders only, nothing wider than A1: holds.** The diff has one write call site, `engine.update` on `sys_user_position` writing `position` alone (`position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:252`). `readLeftBehind` (`:340-367`) only calls `find` on the six other stores and names what it finds. No file in plugin-sharing, plugin-approvals or platform-objects moves. No install or upgrade hook is added: the carry sits inside the `kernel:bootstrapped` handler that already exists (`security-plugin-start-hooks.ts:377`, `:396-404`).
- **Written as the system: holds.** Every read and the write carry the `isSystem` context (`:96`, `:201`, `:244`, `:252`), the spelling the sibling boot passes use.
- **Every organization, no cross-tenant move: holds.** One unscoped read takes the rows naming the old name (`:232`), then one by-id update per row. `organization_id` is never written, the twin is looked up in the row's own organization (`:241`), and the report counts per organization (`:260`). The pass crosses organizations inside one environment by design. It never leaves the kernel's own engine and catalog, so it crosses no environment boundary.
- **Once per boot, not per load: holds.** It runs once in the `kernel:bootstrapped` handler, after the permission-set package backfill and before the catalog reference report, so a moved holder is not reported as naming no position. A package registered into a running kernel does not run it (see ③).
- **Idempotent on restart and partial failure: holds.** A carried name has no row left to read (pinned, `position-renamed-holder-carry.test.ts:135-147`), and a row moved by hand is not on the old name, so it is not read. After a failure the rows already moved stay moved and the next boot reads the rest. What a failure does to the rest of the run is should-fix 5.
- **No duplicate key: holds.** The twin is read first (`:240-249`). The declared unique key `(user_id, position, organization_id)` (`sys-user-position.object.ts:216`) backs the read, and a violation is caught and the row left and named (`:253-258`). For a row with no organization the SQL key is NULL-distinct, so only the read guards it; such a row applies nowhere (ADR-0131 D1), and no pin covers it.
- **Condition 1: holds for the activation ledger.** `switched-off` asks the resolver's own read (`:395-397`, `:443-447`; `resolve-authz-context.ts:1652`) and is pinned both ways (`test:172-187`). Only `position` is written, so the validity window, reason and delegation columns of a row stay (`test:114-133`). The ledger row is a non-holder store and is not moved, so the choice is refusal, the second arm the analysis offered. A package-level disable is also a deactivation, and the carry does not read it (must-fix 1).
- **Condition 2: fails in one arm.** A name a served position holds is refused, pinned for another package and for the environment (`:427-436`, `test:190-202`). The six built-in names are registered by the platform under its own package id (`builtin-positions.ts:157`), so they read as live holders. A position of a disabled package is not refused (must-fix 1). A dead name is judged in ④.
- **Condition 3: holds.** The entry grammar equals the grammar of `name` (`position.zod.ts:169-172` against `identifiers.zod.ts:130-137`). Own name and repeat are refused on one position (`position-renamed-from.ts:28-52`). A name still declared, which covers a cycle, and an old name claimed twice are refused on the `positions` collection (`position-renamed-from.ts:64-98`, `stack.zod.ts:958-959`). The carry judges both again over the one catalog (`:415-436`, `test:223-249`).
- **Clause-② yes (widening): holds.** `PositionSchema` is a closed `strictObject`, so no position that parses on `origin/main` carries `renamedFrom`. Both refinements return early when the key is absent (`position-renamed-from.ts:30`, `:73`), so they refuse nothing that parses today. No `extend`, `pick` or `omit` of `PositionSchema` exists under `packages`, so the added refinement breaks no derived schema.
- **Census: consistent with the one new write.** `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md:215` adds one row for the carry (`update`, elevated). The totals move by exactly one in both files: sites 308 to 309, run-time object name 94 to 95, threading a context 238 to 239, elevated 173 to 174.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves (AGENTS.md Post-Task 3). The changeset is `minor` for `@objectstack/spec` and for `@objectstack/plugin-security` (`.changeset/32983-position-renamed-from-carries-holders.md:2-3`). Correct. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are line-leading in the changeset (lines 6-7) and in the PR body, and the one reader reads both as declared in both places. A `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line is in both. The change is not breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed; the ruling's "ADR-0087 entry" is the `added` projection from the authorable surface (`authorable-surface/identity.json:60`). The rules module is not re-exported, so the public surface grows by the one key. The ADR-0150 addendum is one paragraph under D7 (`docs/adr/0150-...md:288`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **For the maintainer, with the Tier H approval request: the dead-name residual of condition 2 (④).** The carry is a runtime security behaviour on the human floor, so a condition of the ruling is the maintainer's to relax, not the seat's.
- **A marketplace upgrade applied to a running kernel carries nothing until the next restart.** The install door hot-registers the new version (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3185` and the header at `:529`), and nothing fires `kernel:bootstrapped` again. The field precedent carries at that door (`field.zod.ts:2627-2632`). The order scoped this card to the existing start hook, so this is not a defect of this head. It is a gap against the ruling's "when the renamed definition loads" and against the card's own marketplace case, and it needs a card or the maintainer's word. The hand-off should say it.
- **Overlays, not measured.** An ADR-0005 overlay body replaces the package body in the catalog, and the Setup form omits the key (`metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts:430-436`). Whether a Setup save of an overlay keeps `renamedFrom` was not measured. An overlay of the old name that outlives the rename reads as a live environment position, so the carry refuses and the holders keep the old customised position. That direction is closed and loud.
- **The metadata save door accepts the key.** It parses a position with `PositionSchema` (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:169`), so an environment position or an overlay may declare `renamedFrom` through the API although the form omits it. A metadata author gains nothing by it: the same author may already author a position under the dead name itself.
- **Audit, not measured.** Whether plugin-audit records each system update was not measured. The one record this diff itself guarantees is one `info` line (`:470`), which a logger set to `warn` drops.
- Tier H is owed for `docs/adr/`. The `Skills-docs:` follow-up card for `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` is owed outside this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**The dev's flagged judgment: is the activation-ledger evidence for a dead old name sufficient and safe?**

- **What the evidence is.** A ledger row exists only for a position somebody switched on or off: absence of a row means active (`sys-metadata-activation.object.ts:9-13`), and the only writers are the enable and disable actions (`:57`). A row that names no package is read as no evidence (`position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:406`), although that is also how the ledger spells an item the environment authored (`sys-metadata-activation.object.ts:145-153`).
- **Can a package claim an old name whose ledger row is absent or was never written? Yes.** With no row, `others` is empty (`:437`), nothing is switched off, and the one claimant is carried (`:448`). That is the common case, HotCRM's twelve old names among them.
- **A fresh tenant.** The ledger is empty, so every single claim on a name no served position holds is carried. With no holder row on the name it moves nothing.
- **Fail direction: open (carry).** It is closed only for a served live holder, a row that records another package, a switched-off row, a double claim, and a ledger or catalog that cannot be read (the read throws and nothing is written).
- **Sufficient: no.** The ledger records a toggle, not an owner, so the ruling's sentence "a package cannot claim an old name it never owned" is not enforced for a dead name. A closed direction is not buildable from stored state without defeating A1: the ruled use case has no ledger row either.
- **Safe: yes, on one condition that this head does not meet.** A dead name is already free for any package to declare (ADR-0150 D7, one slot per name), and a holder row is a bare name (D8 row R2), so a package that declares the dead name itself holds its stranded rows at once. The open carry therefore grants no power that name reuse does not already grant, provided the carry refuses every name the registry's one-holder rule would refuse the claimant to declare. That holds for a served package, the environment and the built-ins. It does not hold for a disabled package (must-fix 1). The one real difference from name reuse is that the carry is permanent: name reuse leaves the rows where they are, and the carry rewrites them and nothing carries them back.
- **Disposition.** Accept the open direction as a recorded residual once must-fix 1 closes the condition. It deviates from the letter of condition 2, so the seat puts it to the maintainer in plain words (③), and the ADR line says it (should-fix 3).

**The schema files against the ruling: hold.** The key, its grammar and the four parse refusals follow the field precedent's shape (`refuseDishonestRenamedFrom`), with the position grammar where the field uses the field-key grammar. The form omission is recorded with its reason.

**The ADR addendum against its first consumer.** The line states the write, the scope and the refusals. Two of its statements are wider than the code: "another package ... holds" is not true for a disabled package (must-fix 1), and it does not say that a dead name nobody is recorded as owning is carried for its one claimant (should-fix 3).

**First consumer.** The carry is the only reader of the key, and the liveness row grades it `live` with the executor named. Every condition-2 pin runs on a stand-in catalog; the real reader's shapes are where the gaps below were found (must-fix 1, should-fix 4).

Implemented-by: card thread session_016WV4czhuyaTe2ySbAbhCjq
Reviewed-by: domain:spec#3 seat (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER subagent)

Verdict: FAIL

Items:

1. must-fix: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:378-380` and `:427-436`. Condition 2's live-holder arm reads `catalog.list('position')`, and that list hides every position of a disabled package (`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts:515-521`, `:900`, `:931`; pinned at `security-catalog.test.ts:138`). The registry says a disabled package is still installed and still holds its names (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:4677-4678`), and the disabled state is restored in `AppPlugin.start()`, before `kernel:bootstrapped` (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:764`, `:784`). So while package Z is disabled, another package's `renamedFrom` naming Z's position meets no refusal, and Z's holders are moved to the claimant's position in every organization, for good. This is the feature's own scenario (two apps wanted one name, one renamed away) plus a temporary disable, and the claim is standing, so every boot re-judges it. People on a deactivated position also come back active under the new name, which is condition 1. Judge holders, and the claimants for `claimed-twice`, over every installed package, disabled included, and pin both ways: a disabled holder is refused, an uninstalled one is carried. Read, not run.
2. must-fix: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts:385`. The control pins `position: 13` served top-level properties and the new key makes 14, so `Test Core (6/8)` is red on this head (job 131679495396, step "Run this shard's tests", first error `AssertionError: expected 14 to be 13` at `:399`). Move the count with its note, as the field `renamedFrom` did at `:374-375`. The file is not in the diff, and the red is this diff's.
3. should-fix: `docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md:288`. Add one clause: an old name that no installed position holds and no ledger row records under another package is carried for its one claimant, whichever package that is. The PR body's maintainer summary says all three conditions are pinned, and its Acceptance notes say a package can take such a name's stranded holders; the approver should meet the second sentence where the first is (the seat's ACCEPT for the PR body).
4. should-fix: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:385`, `:429`, `:437`. The carry reads `entry.packageId` raw. The real reader stamps a stored environment item with the sentinel `sys_metadata` (`security-catalog.ts:402-403`), and core exports `catalogEntryAddress` so every reader spells the holder one way (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1452-1461`). An environment position is therefore reported as `package "sys_metadata"` (`:222-223`), and the activation door can store the same value for a position (`catalog-activation.ts:885`). Every pin spells the environment as no `packageId` (`position-renamed-holder-carry.test.ts:91-97`), so none exercises the real shape. Normalise through `catalogEntryAddress` and add one pin through `createSecurityCatalogReader`.
5. should-fix: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:256`, `:448`, `:514-524`. A write that fails for any reason other than a unique violation ends the whole run. Later claims are not tried, and the report of the rows already moved in that boot is dropped: the only line is "did not finish". The next boot meets the same row first, so one position-level refusal blocks every later rename on every boot; the agent-ceiling refusal judges an update naming a position for every writer, the system included (`agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts:320-331`). Isolate a failure per claim, and log what moved before it.
6. should-fix: `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1781`. A package whose rehydrate fails is logged and the boot continues, so its positions are absent from the catalog the same way as in item 1, and a standing claim on one of its names would carry its holders. Not measured here. Measure it, and either stand the carry down for that boot or record the limit in the ADR line.
7. nit: `packages/spec/liveness/position.json:40`. The evidence anchors `refuseDishonestPositionRenamedFrom` in `position.zod.ts`, where the name appears only in a comment. The function is at `position-renamed-from.ts:64` and its call at `stack.zod.ts:959`.
8. nit: the position-name grammar is typed three times (`position.zod.ts:170`, `position-renamed-from.ts:14`, `position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:93`) instead of reusing `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` (`identifiers.zod.ts:130`). The carry's copy drops the two-character minimum.
9. nit: `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md:215`. The new row reads `undecidable` for the object because the name arrives through an imported constant. The sibling `invitation-placement.ts` row reads `sys_user_position`, `enabled`. A local literal would let the census count the carry as an elevated write against a tenancy-enabled object.
10. nit: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:415-424`, `:440`, `:445`. A refused name is added to the left-behind set, so "Re-point each in Setup to the renamed position" (`:495`) prints for a rename that was not carried, and on `claimed-twice` for a name that may still be live.
11. nit: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:302`, `:311`, `:197-208`. While any `renamedFrom` stays declared, every boot reads every pending approval request and every pending invitation into memory.
12. nit: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:479-480`. The twin warning tells the administrator to remove the old row. When the row on the new name is a time-boxed delegation, the old row is the durable assignment.
13. nit: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:240-245`. When two replicas boot together, the second reads a row the first already moved as its own twin and reports it as left on the old name. The data is right and the warning is false.

A delta review by the same reviewer is owed on the head that fixes items 1 and 2. Landing also waits for the head's check-runs to finish green (14 in progress when read) and for the Tier H approval.

### ④ Design judgment

**Is `claimant-disabled` the right design?** Yes. A disabled package serves nothing, so moving people onto its position gives them nothing today, and a move is permanent. Refusing keeps the decision with the boot at which the package is enabled, when the old name is judged again against whoever holds it then.

**The ledger read after the normalisation (new item 1).** The activation door stores a position's package as the catalog entry spells it, the environment sentinel included (`catalog-activation.ts:885`). At the round-1 head a ledger row carrying the sentinel refused a package's claim, under a wrong label. At this head `holderOf` turns it into no package and the row is skipped as no evidence (`position-renamed-holder-carry.ts:488-489`), so the same claim is carried. A row with an empty package is ambiguous, because a row written before the column existed looks the same, and round 1 accepted reading it as no evidence. A sentinel row is not ambiguous: it is the one stored record that the environment authored the old name, which is the "or by no package" arm of condition 2. Refusing on it costs the ruled use case nothing, because a package's own old name is never recorded under the sentinel. It is not a must-fix: a dead name is free for any package to declare, so the carry grants nothing that name reuse does not, which is the test round 1 set. It is a should-fix because the delta opened it, no pin holds either reading, and three texts say the opposite.

**The residual, in the words this review would put to the maintainer.** Condition 2 of the ruling says a package cannot claim an old name it never owned. For a name that is still a position, of any installed package (disabled ones included) or of the environment, the head enforces it. For a name that is no position any more it cannot, because the platform keeps no record of who owned a position that no longer exists, except an activation-ledger row for a position somebody once switched on or off. So when no installed position holds the old name and no ledger row records it under another package, the people still assigned to that name are moved to the one position that claims it, whichever package ships that position, and the move is not undone. A ledger row that records the environment's own position does not stop a package's claim. A package that failed to load at a boot does not hold its names for that boot. The case for accepting it: any package may already declare a free position name and take the same people that way. The alternative is no carry without positive evidence of ownership, which would also stop the ruled HotCRM case, whose old names have no ledger row, unless an ownership record is added first.

**The schema files and the ADR against the code.** The entry grammar is now one declaration. The key's docblock and `.describe()` and the ADR line share the clause that new item 1 corrects. Nothing else in the delta's schema or ADR text disagrees with the carry.
